key_insight: A 2k-dimensional real vector space (R^{2k}) is sufficient to exactly encode subset-membership for top-k retrieval tasks: the paper derives tight Minimal Embeddable Dimension (MED) bounds and shows they hold for ℓ2, inner-product, and cosine similarity.
problem_solved: Determines the minimal embedding dimension needed to represent m elements and all subsets of size ≤ k so that top-k membership/ranking can be recovered — resolving how low-dimensional embeddings can be while preserving exact subset membership and ranking under common similarity measures.
method: Theoretical analysis: derive tight MED bounds for ℓ2, inner product, and cosine similarity, showing constructive sufficiency of R^{2k}.
Constructive embeddings: provide explicit vector constructions/proofs that realize top-k subset retrieval in 2k dimensions.
Empirical validation: numerical simulations in more realistic/achievable subset-sampling settings to confirm tightness and robustness of the bounds.
impact: Provides a provable lower bound (and constructive recipe) for embedding dimensionality, enabling practitioners to design smaller, more efficient vector representations and indices for top-k retrieval when k is small — improving storage, speed, and interpretability.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram: elements and subsets mapped to 2k-dimensional vectors (arrows from subsets to points in R^{2k}).
Plot: required embedding dimension vs k with theoretical line MED=2k and empirical curves showing accuracy vs dimension.
Geometry illustration: how ℓ2 / inner-product / cosine similarities preserve ranking in the constructed embedding (vectors and decision boundaries).
Comparison table: summary of tight bounds per similarity measure and key empirical metrics (accuracy, error vs dimension).
paper_title: $\mathbb{R}^{2k}$ is Theoretically Large Enough for Embedding-based Top-$k$ Retrieval
paper_authors: Zihao Wang, Hang Yin, Lihui Liu, Hanghang Tong, Yangqiu Song
